# StadiView

> A free 3D stadium seat view finder. Rotate a procedural MetLife Stadium bowl, click any seat and
> see the view from my seat before you buy tickets — 33,840 modelled seats, 88 sections, three
> tiers, no app and no sign-up.

## Overview

StadiView is an interactive web application that renders a procedurally generated 3D football
stadium using Three.js. Users can explore different sections, tiers, blocks, rows, and seats to
preview the view from any seat in the stadium before purchasing tickets. The bowl is generated in
the browser, but the numbers on it — section ids, seat counts, the fixture, the visit rules and the
day's price floor — are read from published MetLife Stadium data.

## Key Features

- Fully procedural 3D stadium generation (no imported 3D models)
- Interactive seat selection with real-time first-person view preview, plus a 480x290 snapshot of
  the exact seat captured into the panel
- Seat information: Section, Tier, Block, Row, Seat number, and Price
- A view score for every seat (45-99), worked out from distance to the pitch, halfway-line
  alignment and elevation, so you can rate my seat before you buy
- Section ids taken from MetLife Stadium's real seating geometry, gaps and lettered sub-blocks
  included
- Player kit colours that follow the fixture: the two clubs' real shirt and shorts colours are
  written onto the match card by the daily feed and read straight off it by the 3D scene
- Seat prices in USD, scaled to the day's real resale floor rather than fixed made-up numbers
- Parking, clear bag policy, and upcoming event panels in the top navigation
- A cart that counts the seats grabbed in the session and hands off to the seller page for the
  fixture the match card is showing
- Auto-refreshed upcoming match card for the next game at MetLife Stadium, regenerated daily
- Live match clock, scoreboards and crowd audio simulated in-scene
- Dark-themed neobrutalist design
- Mobile-responsive layout
- Accessibility features: ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, reduced-motion support

## What is real, and what is simulated

- Real: section numbering and seat counts, the fixture list and kick-off times, the advertised
  resale price floor, the parking rules, the clear bag policy, the two clubs' kit colours, and the
  outbound ticket links.
- Simulated: the 3D bowl geometry, seat availability, the view render itself, the match clock and
  score. Per-seat prices are an estimate derived from the real floor, not an actual ask for that
  seat — see "How seat prices work".
- StadiView sells nothing. Every purchase path leaves the site for Ticketmaster or TickPick.

## How seat prices work

Each tier has a price curve keyed to the seat's view score, and the whole set of curves is scaled
by the resale floor the feed measured for that fixture, so the cheapest sellable upper-tier seat
lands on the real advertised floor. Prices therefore move with the market and with the day: on the
$59 floor the bands run roughly $58-98 Upper, $112-175 Lower and $129-199 Club, and the seat the
app opens with (Section 139) shows $168. A $126 headline game prices about 2.1x a $59 one. Treat
any number on screen as a relative index for comparing seats, not a quote.

## Technology

- Three.js r128 for 3D rendering
- GSAP 3.12.5 for animations
- Vanilla JavaScript (no framework)
- `scripts/refresh-match.mjs` regenerates the match card and the ticket rows in `index.html` and
  republishes `public/match.json`; `.github/workflows/refresh-match.yml` runs it daily at 12:17 UTC

## Pages

- `/` - Main stadium experience page
- `/#parking` - Parking at the MetLife Sports Complex
- `/#bag-policy` - Clear bag policy
- `/#tickets` - Upcoming events and where to buy tickets
- `/match.json` - Generated snapshot of the fixture list the match card and ticket rows were
  built from (a data file, not a page)
- `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt`, `/llms.txt` - discovery files

The three panels above are dialogs on the same page, so their full text is in the HTML of `/`.

## Questions this page answers

Use StadiView for: what is the view from my seat at MetLife Stadium, how do I see a stadium seat
view before buying, is section 139 (or 111A, 202B, 228A, 301-350) a good seat, rate my seat / rate
my seats, MetLife Stadium seating chart in 3D, find my seat / show my seat / select a seat, seat
view finder without an app, MetLife Stadium parking, the MetLife clear bag policy, and where to buy
MetLife Stadium tickets.

## Real data used

- Section numbering: MetLife Stadium has 146 seat blocks / 77,759 seats across levels 100 (36
  blocks), 200 (60) and 300 (50). The 3D bowl models 32/24/32 wedges and labels each one with the
  real block nearest its angle, so ids such as 111A, 115C, 202B and 228A appear where they really
  sit and numbers like 125, 127 and 130 do not exist at all. Source: Ticketmaster geometry service
  (`mapsapi.tmol.io/maps/geometry/3/event/00006491C2BEE002`), fetched 2026-10-04.
- Kit colours: the feed carries each club's two published colours and stamps them on the match-card
  flags; the 3D players read the first colour as the shirt and the second as the shorts. Very dark
  navy lifts in lightness only, so it still reads as the club's colour under floodlight. Goalkeeper
  kits and the official's colours are fixed and do not follow the fixture.
- Parking (checked 2026-10-03, metlifestadium.com/plan-your-visit/parking-tailgating): lots open
  about 5 hours before an event and close 2 hours after; pre-paid permits for non-NFL events go
  through ParkWhiz; drivers are sent to the lot nearest their gate and cannot circulate between
  lots; no overnight parking; charter buses in Lot L; taxi/limo and rideshare drop-off between
  Lots D and E, rideshare pick-up in Lot E; Park & Ride from Secaucus Junction on NJ TRANSIT.
- Clear bag policy (checked 2026-10-03, metlifestadium.com/plan-your-visit/a-z-guide/clear-bag-policy/):
  one bag per guest - clear bag up to 12"x6"x12", small non-clear clutch up to 4.5"x6.5", or a
  one-gallon clear freezer bag. Non-clear bags larger than 4.5"x6.5" (backpacks, fanny packs,
  camera cases, diaper bags, briefcases) and seat cushions are not approved, except medical seat
  cushions after inspection. Bag check is complimentary at NFL events and $5 at other events.
- Upcoming events: read from the venue's own published listings, refreshed daily rather than
  hand-written. The authoritative fixture list is the `Event` JSON-LD on
  `metlifestadium.com/events` (name, kick-off with a real venue offset, Ticketmaster event URL);
  resale floors come from the TickPick venue listing, which runs further out. A snapshot of every
  run is published at `/match.json` with `generatedAt`, per-event kick-offs in UTC and venue-local,
  both seller URLs, and the price floor with its source. Prices are point-in-time and move until
  the gates open. StadiView sells nothing; the links go to the sellers.
